core.title: Interlocking route resolution returns a structured resolution model, not a bare train identifier
core.given: An interlocking runner exposes a route-resolution operation (resolveTrain)
core.when: the route-resolution operation resolves a route
core.then: the operation returns a structured interlocking-resolution model (InterlockingResolution) defining interlockingId, routeId, trainId, trainPath, category, guardId, resolutionStrategy, and reason — not a bare train identifier.
prefer: Declare the resolution model as an explicit typed structure naming the eight required fields (interlockingId, routeId, trainId, trainPath, category, guardId, resolutionStrategy, reason).
Populate and return the structured model from the route-resolution operation.
avoid: Resolving a route to only a bare train identifier.
Judging category agreement from a digit parsed out of the identity validation instead of the target train's category field.
unless: No interlocking runner with a route-resolution operation is present (the separate runner-existence concern).
core.why: A bare train identifier loses the routeId, guardId, category, resolutionStrategy, trainPath and the human-readable reason needed for trace and projection equivalence.
evidence: A structural check finds a declared resolution model whose recognized fields include all eight required fields whenever an interlocking runner exposes the route-resolution operation.
A reviewer confirms the route-resolution operation returns the structured model (type-level conformance is delegated to the stack's type-safety enforcement, which runs alongside this rule).
A reviewer confirms category agreement is checked against the target train's category field.
verification: Trigger: the interlocking runner exposes the route-resolution operation. Requirement: a declared resolution model exists defining the eight fields interlockingId, routeId, trainId, trainPath, category, guardId, resolutionStrategy, reason; otherwise report that the route is resolved as a bare train identifier.
Which files the check inspects is the per-stack detector's implementation boundary; scan coverage does not exempt runners outside the scan from the obligation.

How the model and its fields are recognized (declaration forms, field collection) is the per-stack detector's concern, not the neutral obligation; equivalent declaration forms that carry the same eight fields all satisfy the check.
The shape check proves existence of the model only; return-type conformance is delegated to the stack's type-safety enforcement, which runs alongside this rule.
Disposition strict, severity 4: a resolution backed only by a bare train identifier is not suppressible and fails CI.

values: an interlocking runner exposes a route-resolution operation

fires: An interlocking runner exposes the route-resolution operation and it returns a bare train identifier.
An interlocking runner exposes the route-resolution operation and no resolution model is declared.
An interlocking runner exposes the route-resolution operation and the resolution model lacks one of the eight required fields.
An existing, unchanged route-resolution operation on an interlocking runner still returns a bare train identifier.
doesNotFire: No interlocking runner or no route-resolution operation exists (the separate runner-existence concern).

neutralityNotes: The domain-model names (interlocking runner, resolveTrain, InterlockingResolution, and the eight field names) are product-domain vocabulary shared by every stack realization of this obligation, so they remain in the core; only the TypeScript declaration forms, the detector's scan path and field-recognition mechanics, the detector/validator/finding ids, the sibling and runs_alongside rule ids, and the language gate are Bun-only. No profile key was needed: the Bun text itself defers scan scope and field recognition to the per-stack detector, and that deference is kept in core.verification, so profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. The rule's strict disposition and severity 4 are carried in core.verification rather than the profile, per the notProfileKeys list.
